name: Refugee Status Determination (CONARE)

requirements.blocker_text: Paraguay has a genuine domestic refugee law -- Refugee Law No. 1938 (2002) -- administered by CONARE (the National Commission for Refugees), a real, named government eligibility body, not an outside-the-law UNHCR-only process as found for several other countries in this dataset. The law applies both the 1951 Refugee Convention's traditional persecution-based definition AND the broader 1984 Cartagena Declaration definition (covering generalized violence, foreign aggression, internal conflict, and massive human rights violations, common in Latin American refugee law but stricter/absent elsewhere in this dataset). Guaranteed protections include non-refoulement, confidentiality, and family unity. Paraguay ratified the 1951 Convention and 1967 Protocol in 1970, and acceded to the 1954 and 1961 Statelessness Conventions in 2012 -- notably becoming, in 2018, the first South American country to adopt a dedicated statelessness-determination framework, addressing possible statelessness in children born abroad to Paraguayan parents.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee status claim with CONARE, which determines eligibility under either the 1951 Convention definition or the broader 1984 Cartagena Declaration definition.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, tied to continued protection needs

sources.title: UNHCR RIMAP -- Paraguay's Refugee Law 1938 (2002), CONARE, 1951 Convention + 1984 Cartagena Declaration standards, 2018 statelessness framework (first in South America)
